title: Regulation (EC) No 767/2009
supported_claim: Feed materials primarily meet nutritional needs and may be used directly, after processing, in compound feed, or as premixture carriers.
limitation: EU market definition; does not classify every ambiguous AOM label or establish global legal status.

title: Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003
supported_claim: Feed additives are substances, microorganisms, or preparations other than feed materials and premixtures, intentionally added for listed functions.
limitation: Authorization is product-, use-, species-, dose-, and time-specific.

title: Recommendation 2011/25/EU
supported_claim: A product cannot simultaneously be a feed material and feed additive in this legal classification; production, purity, safety, mode of use, and functionality must be considered together.
limitation: Non-binding EU guidance; low incorporation rate alone is not decisive and case-by-case assessment remains necessary.

title: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/758
supported_claim: Confirms case-by-case product classification using processing, chemical definition, standardisation, safety, mode of use, and functionality.
limitation: Covers specified products and does not automatically classify unrelated AOM concepts.

title: Regulation (EU) 2022/1104 amending the Catalogue of feed materials
supported_claim: Catalogue entries 13.8.1 and 13.8.2 identify crude glycerine/glycerol and refined glycerine/glycerol as feed materials.
limitation: Catalogue identity includes production and compositional conditions; generic AOM Glycerol still needs scope alignment.

title: List of feeds and feed categories
supported_claim: Feedipedia browsing separates Forage plants, Plant products/by-products, Feeds of animal origin, and Other feeds.
limitation: Category navigation is not a formal ontology, disjointness axiom, or legal product classification.

title: Crops
supported_claim: Crops are cultivated for food, fibre, livestock fodder, or other uses; feed crops are narrower than crops.
limitation: Agricultural terminology does not directly determine AOM feed-material hierarchy.

title: Feed crops
supported_claim: Feed crops are crops cultivated explicitly or primarily for feeding animals and are used as forage.
limitation: Use relations do not identify a particular harvested feed material or processing state.

title: Forage
supported_claim: Forage is plants or plant parts other than separated grain that are fed or grazed and may be fresh, dry, or ensiled.
limitation: Definition describes feed use/material scope, not a disjoint biological plant class.

title: AOM Livestock staging graph
supported_claim: Provides current labels, hierarchy, branch membership, and descendant counts used by the reproducible inventory.
limitation: Current generated graph exposes modelling state and may include defects; placement is not acceptance evidence.

title: Governed livestock source identity
supported_claim: Establishes occurrence and source labels for Glycerol and Pleurotus ostreatus in the ingredient data context.
limitation: Does not by itself establish exact chemical scope, biological material part, regulatory status, or legal feed-product kind.
